(c) At $\theta = \pi/3$, find $\frac{d\theta}{dt}$ given that $\frac{dr}{dt} = -2\sin\theta$.
parsed.solution:
(a) Area $= \frac{1}{2}\int_{\pi/3}^{5\pi/3} \left(4^2 - (3 + 2\cos\theta)^2\right) d\theta$

(b) $\frac{dr}{d\theta} = -2\sin\theta \Rightarrow \frac{dr}{d\theta}\bigg|_{\theta=\pi/2} = -2$

$r\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 3 + 2\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 3$

$y = r\sin\theta \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{d\theta} = \frac{dr}{d\theta}\sin\theta + r\cos\theta$

$x = r\cos\theta \Rightarrow \frac{dx}{d\theta} = \frac{dr}{d\theta}\cos\theta - r\sin\theta$

$\frac{dy}{dx}\bigg|_{\theta=\pi/2} = \frac{dy/d\theta\big|_{\theta=\pi/2}}{dx/d\theta\big|_{\theta=\pi/2}} = \frac{-2\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) + 3\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}{-2\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) - 3\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)} = \frac{-2}{-3} = \frac{2}{3}$

The slope of the line tangent to the graph of $r = 3 + 2\cos\theta$ at $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$ is $\frac{2}{3}$.

— OR —

$y = r\sin\theta = (3 + 2\cos\theta)\sin\theta \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{d\theta} = 3\cos\theta + 2\cos^2\theta - 2\sin^2\theta$

$x = r\cos\theta = (3 + 2\cos\theta)\cos\theta \Rightarrow \frac{dx}{d\theta} = -3\sin\theta - 4\sin\theta\cos\theta$

$\frac{dy}{dx}\bigg|_{\theta=\pi/2} = \frac{dy/d\theta\big|_{\theta=\pi/2}}{dx/d\theta\big|_{\theta=\pi/2}} = \frac{3\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) + 2\cos^2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) - 2\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}{-3\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) - 4\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)} = \frac{-2}{-3} = \frac{2}{3}$

The slope of the line tangent to the graph of $r = 3 + 2\cos\theta$ at $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$ is $\frac{2}{3}$.

(c) $\frac{dr}{dt} = \frac{dr}{d\theta} \frac{d\theta}{dt} = -2\sin\theta \cdot \frac{d\theta}{dt} \Rightarrow \frac{d\theta}{dt} = \frac{dr}{dt} \cdot \frac{1}{-2\sin\theta}$

$\frac{d\theta}{dt}\bigg|_{\theta=\pi/3} = 3 \cdot \frac{1}{-2\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)} = \frac{3}{-\sqrt{3}} = -\sqrt{3}$ radians per second
